summary:
Backend-only verification of the new browser-friendly GET /api/debug/test-push?token= variant against http://localhost:8001 with ADMIN_TRIGGER_PASSWORD=Pt3481pt and EMERGENT_PUSH_KEY=placeholder. Created /app/backend/tests/test_debug_test_push_browser.py (12 tests / 8 classes) covering all six spec points plus regression + import checks. All 38 pytest tests pass (12 new + 26 pre-existing, 0 failures). Spec results: (a) GET no ?token → HTTP 401, Content-Type text/html, body contains 'Wrong password' ✓. (b) GET ?token=wrong → HTTP 401 HTML 'Wrong password' ✓. (c) GET ?token=Pt3481pt → HTTP 200 text/html, contains '

QuakeGuard test push

', badge='not delivered' (placeholder key, as expected), 'Recipients: 12' line with integer, 'Push delivered: False', and 'Error: EMERGENT_PUSH_KEY missing or invalid' ✓. (d) POST with X-Admin-Token: Pt3481pt → HTTP 200 application/json {recipients:int, push_delivered:false, push_error:'EMERGENT_PUSH_KEY missing or invalid'} — backward compat intact ✓. (e) POST no header → HTTP 401 JSON {detail:'Invalid or missing X-Admin-Token'} — backward compat intact ✓. (f) Verified via regex over server.py: exactly ONE 'async def _run_test_push' and exactly TWO 'await _run_test_push(' call-sites (POST line 217, GET line 239) ✓. Regression: GET /api/debug/devices → 200 with device_count=12/push_key_status='placeholder'/admin_password_configured=true/devices[] ✓; POST /api/trigger-alert with X-Admin-Token → 200 broadcast ✓; POST /api/register-push upsert still visible in /debug/devices (returns 500 locally because placeholder key makes upstream 401 which server re-raises as 500 — pre-existing behavior, DB upsert happens first) ✓; legacy POST/GET /api/status ✓. Imports: server.py imports Query and HTMLResponse; module parses cleanly (ast.parse OK); no lint errors on /app/backend/server.py.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: The GET variant intentionally accepts the password via query string. Correctly documented in the docstring — but the query string will leak into access logs / browser history / referrer headers. Consider rotating ADMIN_TRIGGER_PASSWORD after each browser-based test, or add server-side redaction of ?token from access logs (non-blocking; already noted in code comment).

server.py: /api/debug/test-push (both GET and POST) has no rate-limit; a leaked password would allow unlimited broadcast pushes to every registered device. Consider a naive in-memory throttle (carried over from iteration_10, still non-blocking).

server.py: HTML page interpolates result values via f-string without escaping. Recipients / push_delivered are ints/bools so safe, but push_error comes from an exception .detail (server-controlled) or str(e). If an upstream ever surfaces a message containing HTML, it will render inline. Consider html.escape() around {result['push_error']} for defense-in-depth (non-blocking).
server.py: response models for /api/debug/devices and POST /api/debug/test-push remain untyped dicts (carried from iteration_10).
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_debug_test_push_browser.py (created — 8 test classes / 12 tests covering GET no-token 401 HTML, GET wrong-token 401 HTML, GET correct-token 200 HTML with headline+badge+recipients+push_delivered+error line, POST bc-compat JSON, POST no-header 401 JSON, shared _run_test_push helper wiring, regression on /debug/devices + /trigger-alert + /register-push + /status, and Query/HTMLResponse imports + AST parse)
seed_data_creation: One TEST_regr_<hex> device registered via POST /api/register-push during regression run (upsert visible in /debug/devices — device_count now 12). Left in db.push_devices as inert broadcast recipient (placeholder key ⇒ upstream never called).
context_for_next_testing_agent:
GET /api/debug/test-push?token=Pt3481pt is browser-friendly and returns HTML. Password in query string is intentional per user request (can't easily send POST + header from their browser). EMERGENT_PUSH_KEY is 'placeholder' locally so both GET and POST variants will always report push_delivered=false / push_error='EMERGENT_PUSH_KEY missing or invalid' — this is EXPECTED, not a bug. To assert the badge, use regex on 'Recipients:\s*(\d+)' and check the literal strings '

QuakeGuard test push

', 'not delivered' (or 'delivered' with a real key), 'Push delivered: False|True', 'EMERGENT_PUSH_KEY missing or invalid'. POST /api/debug/test-push still requires header X-Admin-Token: Pt3481pt (unchanged). /api/register-push returns 500 (not 201) locally because upstream 401 is re-raised — DB upsert still succeeds first, so the new user_id will appear in /api/debug/devices. Do not assert 201 without checking upstream key.
rca_of_issue: N/A — all six spec points passed on first assertion pass. The single initial test failure (test_register_push_upserts asserting 201) was a test-only bug on my side: register-push returns 500 with placeholder EMERGENT_PUSH_KEY because server.py:97 converts upstream 401 to 500. Pre-existing behavior verified against test_push_broadcast.py which asserts (201,500). Test corrected to check status in {201,500} + verify upsert via /debug/devices. Total 38/38 pass.
